English Text (msgid):
Print Format Help

Introduction

Print Formats are rendered on the server side using the Jinja Templating Language. All forms have access to the doc object which contains information about the document that is being formatted. You can also access common utilities via the frappe module.

For styling, the Boostrap CSS framework is provided and you can enjoy the full range of classes.

References

  1. Jinja Templating Language
  2. Bootstrap CSS Framework

Example

<h3>{{ doc.select_print_heading or "Invoice" }}</h3>
<div class="row">
	<div class="col-md-3 text-right">Customer Name</div>
	<div class="col-md-9">{{ doc.customer_name }}</div>
</div>
<div class="row">
	<div class="col-md-3 text-right">Date</div>
	<div class="col-md-9">{{ doc.get_formatted("invoice_date") }}</div>
</div>
<table class="table table-bordered">
	<tbody>
		<tr>
			<th>Sr</th>
			<th>Item Name</th>
			<th>Description</th>
			<th class="text-right">Qty</th>
			<th class="text-right">Rate</th>
			<th class="text-right">Amount</th>
		</tr>
		{%- for row in doc.items -%}
		<tr>
			<td style="width: 3%;">{{ row.idx }}</td>
			<td style="width: 20%;">
				{{ row.item_name }}
				{% if row.item_code != row.item_name -%}
				<br>Item Code: {{ row.item_code}}
				{%- endif %}
			</td>
			<td style="width: 37%;">
				<div style="border: 0px;">{{ row.description }}</div></td>
			<td style="width: 10%; text-align: right;">{{ row.qty }} {{ row.uom or row.stock_uom }}</td>
			<td style="width: 15%; text-align: right;">{{
				row.get_formatted("rate", doc) }}</td>
			<td style="width: 15%; text-align: right;">{{
				row.get_formatted("amount", doc) }}</td>
		</tr>
		{%- endfor -%}
	</tbody>
</table>

Common Functions

doc.get_formatted("[fieldname]", [parent_doc]) Get document value formatted as Date, Currency, etc. Pass parent doc for currency type fields.
frappe.db.get_value("[doctype]", "[name]", "fieldname") Get value from another document.

English Text (msgid): One entry on the dock. `link_type` says what kind of thing it opens, and each kind answers the two questions a click asks -- which page comes up and which shell comes up beside it -- in its own way. A `Sidebar` row *is* the shell: it selects that sidebar and opens its landing route. A `Workspace` row opens a page and derives its shell from the module that owns it. A `URL` row leaves the desk and has no shell at all. Every row also carries its own `icon` and `title`, so the rail reads the way its author wrote it -- blank at an upper layer means inherit. What a row points at *is* its identity, and none of it is stored: re-labelling cannot detach a row from itself, and re-pointing is not an edit but a different row. The same rows at all three layers -- the app's own dock, the site's arrangement and one person's -- told apart by the parent `Dock`, never by the row.
Description / Note: Description of a DocType

English Text (msgid): One layer of one app's dock. Three of them share this table, told apart by `app`, `user` and `standard`: the app's own dock, which an app ships as an exported document and a developer authors; the site's arrangement of it, curated by a Workspace Manager and applying to everyone; and one person's own, applied last and winning. A dock belongs to an app, so arranging ERPNext's rail does not touch frappe's -- and a layer is addressed by app plus user rather than by user alone. Same shape at all three, because the rows are identical and the parent is what says whose they are; see `Custom Sidebar`, which layers a sidebar the same way in a table of its own.
Description / Note: Description of a DocType

English Text (msgid): One ordered list holding both references to base items (`added` unset -- non-empty fields override, empty fields mean no opinion) and items this layer added (`added` set -- full items, rendered as they stand). Row order is the arrangement; base items not named here keep their base order and follow the ones that are, which is how a newly installed app's items still reach someone who has already reordered.
Description / Note: Description of the 'Sidebar Items' (Table) field in DocType 'Custom Sidebar'
